text: This armored bufonid is always ready to leap into battle... as long as that battle is really, really close. In a pinch, it can leap multiple times and eventually reach the battle.
The peafowl is renowned for its stunning colors and plumage.
Anima is a fundamental force that infuses the Shadowlands. It flows through many creatures, but is also traded, bartered for, and fought over.
This sun-dappled courser gallops on lightbeams with carefree abandon.
Its bite is definitely worse than its bark-like gurgling sound.
Fed by victory and hardened by glory, this snail is nothing less than a tribute to mastery.
In the Dream, sometimes the myth is more real than its basis.
This rare breed of dragonhawk is a mark of honor in the Horde, gifted by the blood elves. It reflects your tireless effort to amass a small army of mounts.
Once symbols of conquest, these war-bears now stride again, reborn through Nalorakk's blessing and the renewed spirit of the Amani.
The extra-light equipment on this chromatic rylak allows it to swoop and glide through the clouds easily, free from the bounds of the land below.
Some people say that riding an ashhide mushan will result in favorable health and increased prosperity. These people are called "mount vendors."
A loyal creature of Thalassian nobility, it finds comfort holed up in the Magisters' Terrace.
Considered the Top Dog among Stix's Junkyard Hyenas, it boasts a bite force strong enough to crush whatever - or whoever - Gallywix wants disposed of.
Its long, serrated limbs drip with the blood of its enemies and/or mate.
Gottum collects spawns of Krag'wa from all around the Frogmarsh, but only the most bulbous are used as mounts.
Thoroughly trained in how to snort, trot, and stomp on the faces of its enemies.
The fanciest of all of the horses.

Fighting her corrupted handlers this pack mother freed herself and her pups. However, freedom from their handlers did not free them from the void in this lost place. She taught her pups to be even more dangerous beasts, and they now stalk throughout Orgrimmar fetching her food as all compete to survive.
Difficult to build and to maintain, these hogs more than make up for their expense through sheer cool factor.
Rumored to be favored by SI:7 for night missions due to its dark coat.
A Glimmerfur's coat takes on properties of its environment much like a camouflage. Patterns of bright blue skies and majestic white clouds have earned this glimmerfur the nickname "Skypaw."
The Snapvines have always been dangerous, but we never realized that the deep variants were independent, and could fly. This Snapvine is always wanting to see more of the world and be fed.

After the Thunder King's fall, his lingering thunder merged with the spirit of a white dragon. It strides on azure lightning, clouds swirling in its wake-where tyranny once reigned, now guardian light remains.
The fires blaze on, in the steed's heart and soul, now take to the sky as a sight to behold.
Some Goblins affectionately refer to trained hyenas as 'Growlers.' This one is fond of digging.
A swamp-dwelling subspecies of pterrordax known to feast on young bloodfeasters.
It's so wiggly! Just looking at it move is chaotic and unnerving.
A savage K'arroc particularly well-suited to prowling the perpetual twilight of K'aresh.
Winter Harvesthogs are primarily nocturnal creatures. They are slightly slower than other harvesthogs, but their endurance is unmatched.
Take to the skies on a glittering, shimmering, pearlescent butterfly.
Stabled in the Icecrown Citadel to serve the Lich King's most favored minions.
Until it head-butts you below the belt, it has not truly accepted you as its rider.
Dragonhawks are among the deadliest known predators. They are able to spot prey from great distances, rush in, and rend with both talon and beak.
The Kor'kron Juggernaut is a weapon of unbridled destruction, born from the mind of Garrosh Hellscream and made real by his engineers.
Larger than most of its kin, this vulture has shown sick and strong beasts alike why they need to fear the skies.
The Klaxxi ride massive scorpions into battle against their enemies.  A carapace hardened by amber provides superior protection while on the battlefield.
The black serpents of N'Zoth are the harbingers of his ultimate vision becoming reality. Only those servants or enemies that can tread this space have any chance of wrangling them.
One of the gronnlings of Tanaan Jungle caught in the eruption of fel energies unleashed by Gul'dan, and now beholden to an unquenchable lust for chaos.

In life, Blanchy appeared to be an affectionate, well-behaved horse of excellent disposition and appetite. What evils must she have committed in secret to have earned her place among the condemned souls of Revendreth?
Subsists almost entirely on a diet of frozen berries. Though it finds slow off-worlders equally tasty.
Due to the otherworldly energies that irradiated Draenor, these creatures can shift through space at will. As such, they are rarely seen... until it is too late.
Though it was once created to defend the Sepulcher of the First Ones, with its primary function now completed, it now obediently follows your command.
When fallen heroes are raised into undeath, so too are their horses.
A rarity amongst the tallstrider breeds of Kalimdor, but easily recognized by its pungent dead seaweed aroma.
Optimized shredder designed for maximum shredding efficiency.
A ship unlike any other, held aloft by a gift from an unknown kraken-faced god of the deeps.
It was said that this invention was modeled after the likeness of a very wealthy goblin. Although others don't really see the resemblance.
Even the Draconic Native Association tests proved inconclusive in determining if the albino drake is related to a known dragonflight. -Breanni
The House of the Chosen train their mounts in all manner of difficult circumstances, so that no matter the battle, they will never falter.
The fate of all horse mounts.
It feeds on your thoughts, even the ones you are thinking as you read this.

This demonic machine was designed by Chief Engineer Ulzik as an experiment in cross-dimensional traversal. Despite many deaths during testing, Ulzik remained confident that this vehicle would reveal secrets of the universe previously unknowable.
This daughter of the great direhorn loa, Torcali, never lost faith that her keeper would help her grow to her full potential.
I demand speed, grace and discipline on the battlefield. This one will serve nicely. -Eressea Dawnsinger
Cherished for their heavy carrying capacity and steady gait, these stalwart beasts are the mount of choice for most native Pandaren.
A gift from the Council of Six for saving Azeroth from the threat of the Legion once more.
The light from the saddle helps attract prey to this corrupted behemoth.
These resilient scavengers can survive for months in the wastes of Vol'dun with scarce access to food and water.
The pride of the Silvermoon Court, these hawkstriders are prized for their vibrant red plumage and purebred elegance.
As Raszageth's storms abated, this aquatic breed of salamanther was among the many wonders to settle among the shores in their wake.
Born capable of sniffing out concentrations of arcane energy, this noble cat was presented with thanks to a proven ally of the nightborne.
The majestic eagle is a symbol of pride for the Highmountain tribes. This great beast's ability to carry tauren on their backs speaks to the sheer strength and size of the creatures of Highmountain.
The Barak Tor'ol ram's thick bony skull and massive horns make it the ideal mount for charging through groups of armored enemies.
While often aggressive, some Harrowers can be tamed and taught to aid in defensive military techniques. This Harrower looks over the Stormarion Core to ensure none can breach it.
Windsteeds are incredibly gentle and easy to train... if you can catch one.
They say that proto-drakes can smell fear. This iron-bound monster FEEDS off of it.

The presence of this majestic Pandaren rabbit spirit brings joy and happiness and is heralded as a wonderful omen. Legend says that in its eyes, you can glimpse the greatest happiness of your life, even if it is yet to come.

Traders quickly found them a very capable ally when facing the dangers of Northrend and beyond. They also learned that the bears of the Grizzly Hills were fiercely loyal. Especially to those who keep Emperor salmon at hand.
Azure Cloud Serpents are believed by the Pandaren to be harbingers of good fortune.
Sylvanas lost a part of herself the day Arthas took her life, and the darkness within her grew to fill the void.
This ferocious beast, renowned among wyvern handlers, was one of the first mounts chosen to take part in the Horde's Dominance Offensive.
Captured in the snows of Alterac Valley, this bloodthirsty hunter now roars for the Alliance.
Gravewings know no fear and are nearly indestructible -- perfect for an assault on the Maw.
A beloved mount in southern Pandaria, the jungle crane is known for its speed and agility honed over a lifetime of avoiding Krasari tigers.
Raptors have spread to nearly all of the lands of Azeroth. It is uncertain whether the trolls led them or followed them.
Prized for its intelligence, this breed of talbuk can be trained to execute defensive kicks and gorings in battle.
Because sharp teeth and claws weren't enough.
Felfire is deadly to the touch.  Luckily, the hawk can suppress the flames, choosing not to incinerate its rider in an emerald effigy.
Was I a good boy? the soul asked Zovaal. "No. I'm told you were the worst."
The Alliance uses these ravenous snail mounts to traverse over any obstacle in battlefields.
The most aggressive nether drakes were awarded those heroes who showed significant prowess and commitment in the gladiatorial arena.
The Snapvines have always been dangerous, but we never realized that the deep variants were independent, and could fly. The distinct, bold coloring means the creature has eaten recently.
Patient and strong, the Elekk exemplify the Draenei attitude towards the hardships of life.
Stubborn until broken, these underwater mounts provide the swiftest means of travel around the depths of Vashj'ir.

The mammoths of the Ohn'ahran Plains are unaccustomed to carrying people, as their centaur neighbors do not typically ride mounts. They can learn to bear riders, however. Some even do so enthusiastically.
A rare breed of Dragonhawk that soars the Thalassian skies on azure wings after having escaped from the Sunwing Rookery.
The wilderlings are benevolent, magical creatures of Ardenweald, and are drawn to souls that are strong and pure.
A special creation of Lord Illidan gifted to his most trusted demon hunters.
Even infusion with demonic magics could not break the spirits of these majestic beasts, and their twisted forms were never integrated into the Legion's service.
The hide of a highland elderhorn is incredibly thick. Never in recorded history has a highland elderhorn even blinked in response to insults thrown at them.
Despite their docile nature, talbuks have been known to gore seasoned warriors to death when threatened.
The only reason for time is so that everything doesn't happen at once.
No adult knows why some ottuks are white, but any tuskarr child can tell you: it's because they eat too much snow.
Considered one of Azeroth's perfect predators, these agile beasts can sprint through dense forests without making a sound.
Native to Hyjal, these mischievous tree-dwellers underwent a startling transformation when the Firelands made its appearance in the region.
Mages celebrating Noblegarden turned their ordinary festive decor into floating spectacles, only to have them stolen by an angry druid.
Its bracers seem to be a bit snug.
This dinosaur still harbors the rage of its ancestors from the Zandalari Invasion.
These harrowers are attracted to the constant battle cries and bloodshed across Slayer's Rise.
Swift as the storm and sharp as lightning, these sacred eagles bear the mark of Akil'zon, carrying their riders on the winds of her blessing.
The Tol'vir sorcerer Azj'Aqir was said to possess a scepter that would allow him to control a Qiraj battle tank outside of its Silithus home.
This wild talbuk found among the ruins of Argus has survived and persevered through decades of strife.
Warhounds find comfort in conflict, and the Contest of Conquest is the perfect place to find these beasts honing their abilities.
When an armored phalynx is forged, stewards clap their hammers together in reverence of the skill required in its creation.
Few talbuks managed to remain unscathed despite the Legion's exploitation of their homeworld. Their tenacity is befitting of a noble steed.
Normally placid beasts, these intelligent animals form a strong bond with their riders, making them loyal and fearless in battle.
Most undead steeds have their riders chosen for them. Valiance, on the other hand, chooses its own rider.
This gift of the silvery winds is only bestowed upon those that search high and low for the wisdom of Bastion.
Hogrus was first seen by Emperor Shaohao on the third day of his meditation, and is considered by the Pandaren to be a sign of good fortune to come to those who take action.
The crane is a symbol of wisdom and nobility, their ability to carry us into the skies is nothing short of miraculous. - Jaluu the Generous
Verdant skitterflies are the perfect mount for the scouts of the Dragonscale Expedition scouts, as they are fast and blend into the foliage of the Dragon Isles.
Recovered from the Cauldron's bleachers during a particularly gruesome clash. When asked if it was a dud, Torq's operator simply replied: 'Probably?'
Many bars of gildenite are required to forge one of these sparkling mounts, but the sight of them alone is worth the gathering time.

Chameleonic creatures can oftentimes adapt their cells to match the color of the outside world. This snapdragon adopted this ability, but only to match the contents of their stomach; taking the phrase 'you are what you eat' to a whole new level.

Patents of lineage are used to demarcate the history and value of thoroughbred undercrawlers in Kaheti high society. This practice can prove somewhat difficult when said undercrawlers are prone to the sudden consumption of their record-keepers.
A true explorer never stays in one place for long. Having a reliable packbeast with a strong back and sturdy legs is essential for travel.
Some cannot be held back or restrained. Scorching Valor will seek greatness and only serve those who can serve their pursuit.
Images of this breed are often found on kegs of watered-down dwarven brew.
When fallen heroes are raised into undeath, so too are their horses.
This rather rambunctious Pango escaped from the Witherbark Tribe after having its armor affixed. Finders keepers!
These fearsome mounts have a habit of suddenly breaking out into dance amid battle, much to the annoyance of their riders.

The Blood Queen's mastery of the sanguine arts allowed her to conjure a fearsome servant to bear her into battle. Adorned in livery suited to her court, it is masked with a fearsome visage, and adorned with wings and claws to bring to mind its master's wrath.
These elusive fish prefer to skulk in the deepest reaches of the Great Sea, searching the darkness for food.
Bitter rival to The Bone Melter, this creeper was ousted from their lair near Manaforge Omega after a crushing defeat. It now seeks to learn from the one that dethroned its greatest foe.
This creature hungers for battle with the contemptible Horde.
Even an unarmored tauralus is a valuable ally in battle, its enormous horns capable of piercing even plate armor.

Sargeras' own hound was maybe once a felstalker, but over the years the Dark Titan reforged and reshaped his companion into something much more powerful. When, at last, he was pleased with his creation, he set about creating more of the hounds, and imbuing them with shadow and flame.
I still don't get why they fly faster when you put armor on them. -Drakma
Native to Draenor, these wolves are preferred by the Mag'har for their ferocity, loyalty, and for something to snuggle on those cool winter nights.
Most lava flows. This lava charges.
Legends state that the Pureblood line may be traced back to the very creation of the Firelands.
What it lacks in safety features it more than makes up for in speed and style.  Not for the faint of heart.
It's the second biggest murloc you've ever seen!
When being a courageous member of the Alliance doesn't strike the right amount of fear into your opponent, add a giant spider.
This drake visited many heroes in their dreams before joining your cause.
Although many precious gems have been corrupted by void energies in horrific visions, Master Jewelcrafters can still utilize them to craft mighty panther steeds.
Sharp at both ends and crafty in the middle. Leave it to the trolls to think this was a good idea.
In life, it could not be tamed, but necromancy and esoteric binding rituals have now combined to bend this indomitable creature to its rider's will.
Some daydreams are filled with wondrous possibilities, but shatter when reminded of reality's limitations. Some dreams are not so burdened, even when they carry a rider.
Flayedwings are a necessary force in the cycle of life for the Shadowlands, acting as both prey and predator for the harsh environment of Maldraxxus.
When a night elf's mount perishes, it is custom for the rider to keep one of the saber's great fangs as a token of remembrance.
A deadly combination of fel and horse.
Talbuks, native to Argus, have evolved chitinous plates to survive the decades of ceaseless war that ravages the landscape.
The one and only source for the rare culinary ingredient: cursed bacon.
This raptor breed was originally cultivated by the Drakkari, but has since been adopted by the Darkspear tribe in Northrend.
Infused with acidic blood through a terrifying ritual, you can feel your control over this beast is tenuous at best.
Through the Sacred Flame, whispers of dark carry you to battle.
Some of our brethren prefer horses, but the hawkstrider will always be the true symbol of Silvermoon. -Winaestra
Trained using ancient dracthyr methods, these armored vorquin are the pinnacle of tactical mounted ground warfare.
Patient and strong, the Elekk exemplify the Draenei attitude towards the hardships of life.
The tauralus is considered courageous, though scholars of Maldraxxus have long wondered if their lack of fear is simply due to the tiny size of their brains.
This monstrous, flesh-eating bat is the undisputed ruler of the night skies.
This (relatively) domesticated silithid is at home only in the desert sands of Ahn'Qiraj.
It may look menacing right now, but it's actually kind of cute when it's asleep.
The dwarves value their ram companions for their fearlessness charging into battle.
Marrowfang, Bonefang's progeny, was respected by Amarth the Harvester for her insatiable appetite, even if it disrupted any experiments that the sadistic commander wanted to run.
A strikingly colored Dragonhawk admired across Quel'Thalas, its vivid red wings cutting bright arcs through the skies as it glides with smooth, effortless grace.
The preferred vehicle for assassinations, they make no sounds when flying - really great for sneaking up on people.

With the death of the Jailer and the ascension of a new Arbiter, the Shadowlands is returning to its great Purpose. Some deathwalkers recognize the role that mortal heroes have played, and are willing to serve as mounts.
Stolen from the Arathi Basin stables, this fire-hearted charger now steeds for the Horde.
While dark and ominous is the preferred aesthetic of those who reside in Revendreth, there are some who still favor gleaming luster.
Heroes who proved their might in the gladiatorial arenas during the Cataclysm were awarded the most exceptional of the twilight drake broods.
If you try to give it a belly scratch, you're asking for trouble.
The Qiraji War Tank has only been seen recently during the Call of the Scarab, could this hint at a resurfacing of the deadly creatures?
These drakes feel at home in the depths of the earth and the far reaches of the sky.
...as though welcomed by the wind itself.
Male rams will often smash their thick skulls against each other for hours to impress a female. In that way, they're very similar to dwarves.
It never pays to leave a live dragon out of the equation.
A properly accelerated gnome in battle is a thing of terrible beauty. - High Tinker Mekkatorque
Coursers make for excellent steeds. Just don't try to dismount from their front.
Riverwallows are one of the heartiest beasts on Draenor, resulting in their increased stamina and distinctive coloring.
Despite their docile nature, talbuks have been known to gore seasoned warriors to death when threatened.
Riding Yaks are bred to be slimmer and more agile than their kin.
Once plentiful, only three seekers remain on Azeroth after generations of battling the corruption of the cosmos.
Vengeful spectres abound in the spirit realm surrounding Dazar'alor.
Razorwings can be seen throughout Korthia, making their nests on high hills and in trees.
Bred from the fiercest stock anywhere and guaranteed not to bite (much).
Named for their resemblance to the bright berries made into arcwine, these proud cats have a keen awareness of the ley lines that travel beneath them.
This horse has been irreversibly scarred by the Legion's corrupt magics.
Forged in a fiery hatred, the offspring of a nightmare and a dream, this steed feeds on grains grown with the tears of your enemies.
Bred specifically to honor those heroes who showed significant courage and persistence facing the dangers in Northrend.
Warmth and hope emanate from this great creature, which glows like a sunrise over the mountains.
The blood of your enemies won't even show up, blends right in.
The blood-red coloration of these creatures is ideal for hiding in large coral formations.
Gottum's expansion into export markets was inevitable with news of the Trading Post reaching even into the depths of the Frogmarsh.
A few of the Argent Crusade's swiftest mounts were awarded to those members of the Horde who performed exceptionally during the tournament in Icecrown.
You built this yourself, you should be proud, even though it's smoky, sparky, and loud.
This beast glows with a radiance no void could suppress.
A somewhat surprising choice of mount, the Council of Dornogal assures you riding it is safe. Mostly.
This lynx's barding has had most of its insignia ripped off. The one remaining tag reads, "Dauntless".
During the war of the elemental lords, Cormaera were often used as beasts of burden for the Firelord's most loyal lieutenants.
The most devastating technology money can buy.
The talbuks of Argus have grown long, coarse fur of brilliant colors that reflects the hues of their broken planet.
By fire be purged the obstacles in your path!
The yellow scouting ottuk love to hide and they blend in well to their surroundings. When not 'playing' hide and seek with their riders, they are perfect companions when scouting enemy encampments.
Trained to accept only champions of the Light as a rider.
This gryphon was the runt of its pride, left behind when its brethren were sent for training. Today, however, it is ready to prove its worth.
This soul eater's gaze unnerves you. Best not meet its eyes for too long.
The Army of the Light could only save so many of Argus' native species; countless numbers were lost to chaos.
Only those heroic souls who surmount every challenge the mogu tyrants place before them can proudly fly the skies on a war-prepared skyscreamer.
An alpha member of the herd, this elekk is a prime example of the mighty creatures which thunder through Northern Nagrand.
These drones will swarm anyone who dares approach their queen uninvited.
The Legion experimented with the corruption of many different types of wildlife, such as this fiery bird species from a molten world.
This aircraft will help you delve straight into adventure, if it doesn't explode!
They say that proto-drakes can smell fear. This iron-bound monster FEEDS off of it.
Its tail smells like campfire but its breath smells like brimstone.
The aquilon can rapidly transport aspirants, stewards, and even ascended to a location. Hey, sometimes your wings get tired.
A darker look for the "Motion By Emotion" magic broom series of mounts. Fans of this color know that it looks good regardless of the time of day.
Once a year, a rift in time appears, and strange things occur. The Illidari scouts and Doomwalker were quite surprised to find themselves in Tanaris.
The rest be forgotten to walk upon the ground, clipped wings and shame. -Word of the Raven
The Forsaken believe that without a purpose, even beasts of burden suffer in undeath.
Packaged upgrades include; dual-lantern fog lights, emergency brew keg, and genuine Tanji leather seat.  - Turtlemaster Odai

The Countess maintains a small stable of elegantly adorned gargon mounts for her sole use. Many a rival has been taken in by the finery to their peril as she personally oversees their deadly training.
Flying true even in the harshest conditions, this lightning-infused rook was trained to soar through the skies of the Isle of Dorn and into the depths below.
Never... ever... EVER... let it smell bacon on you.
Iron Horde beastmasters bred this rylak for war and then girded it for battle in black steel and smoldering flame.
Like most undead creatures, it did not choose its fate.
The fearsome beast ridden by Astaroth himself is now yours to command.
An alpha member of the herd, this kodo is a prime example of the mighty creatures which thunder through the Southern Barrens.
A gilded variant of the Arcane Guardian, most often seen guarding the more opulent districts of Silvermoon City.
Warmth and serenity emanate from this great creature, which glows like the cloudless sky of a summer afternoon.
The most precious cargo in all Ardenweald, the wildseeds, are cradled by this lovingly-crafted cart. It is imbued with anima to allow it to hover over the ground.
Only those most esteemed by the Enlightened are trusted with the reins of this rare cervid.
Surviving on Argus is not an easy task. Its leathery hide scarred by fel corruption, this mana ray is prone to fits of aggression, moreso than usual.
How do you not fall right through that thing? -Maztha
A rare albino of the species first spotted in Desolace.  The centaur claim that a white kodo is a harbinger of doom.
What started as a rideable mining and logging machine devolved quickly into chaos when engineers asked themselves if they could make it any cooler.
Flameward Hippogryphs revel in the defeat of Ragnaros, Lord of Fire.
Fennimore Quigley is credited with milking the first camel and breaking the record for "longest unintentional flight," all in the same afternoon.
Male rams will often smash their thick skulls against each other for hours to impress a female. In that way, they're very similar to dwarves.
The hardest winds begin with a gust and a flap.
Nothing frightens a kodo like seeing a bear with antlers.
A corpse is a corpse, of course of course.
Begifted to a young Tol'vir Princess, this ornate jeweled statue was brought to life by the Gemseers of Ramkahen.
Hippogryphs are highly intelligent, sentient beings; far more than mere "mounts."
This pterrordax was so eager to take to the skies that its handler couldn't finish training it.
This ebony cloud serpent is a lightning-wreathed vision of such rarity as to have driven many mortals to madness.
The elusive Ruby Butterfly is highly sought after by Twilight Witches.
Her white glow upon their silvered fur, her bright-blue gaze in their moonlit eyes. Oh, how the moons smile on these creatures. -Mother Kalo'thera, High Priestess of Elune, A Blessing in Hajiri
An alpha member of the herd, this elekk is a prime example of the mighty creatures which thunder through Northern Nagrand.
Favorite pets of the ancient Mogu princes, Quilen make loyal and fearless companions and mounts.
Otherwise known as The Flame Woof, the Fetcher of the Igneous, Molten Core's Best Friend, Forgehound Maximus, the Best Fiery Boy, and "oh no is that an AXE on his face!?"
They are lethal at eight months, very lethal. -Hemet Nesingwary Jr.
A beast from an unknown world within the Twisting Nether, tamed through brutal and relentless will.
Can howl loudly enough to be heard for miles.
Some legends say the draenei first befriended the elekk after one of the beasts saved an injured scout from a pack of vicious podlings.
They are not native to Northrend, but they have adapted extremely well to the cold. -Mei Francis

Reshkigaal bided her time as her kin each tried their hand at usurping the Banished One. She sought to attack when he was distracted, but the Jailer's spies had been tracking her. With their warning and aid, the Jailer prevailed.
The Horde had dragons, we had the gryphons. We won that war. - Ilsa Blusterbrew

A few Silvermoon Magisters once dedicated their arcane thesis to the study of infusing local flora with arcane-flecked pollen and the effects it had on pollinator species. To the Grand Magister, it was a success. To Silvermoon's Gardeners, it was not.
Only expert flesh-stitchers who have demonstrated mastery over the magics of Maldraxxus are powerful enough to construct a deathroc of this size.
This clefthoof has seen ages pass, witnessing everything and patiently teaching many to ride.
Liberated from the Qalashi and harnessed by your ingenuity (and your harness), this magmammoth is ready to lava stomp wherever you want to go.
It takes unflagging patience and a gentle touch to train obstinate mountain goats for riding.
As one of the last remaining polyps of an elusive creature, this aurelid is at home in the water as much as the air.
Packaged upgrades include; dual-lantern fog lights, emergency brew keg, and genuine Tanji leather seat.  - Turtlemaster Odai
Stubborn and rebellious, this wilderling is loyal to very few. But those few are bonded for life.
Once thought to be extinct except in the far north. Highly sought by those preparing for winter.
Hop aboard this flying carpet to see the shining, shimmering, and splendid world of Azeroth, wonder by wonder.
Basking in the power of M'uru has strengthened its will.
His blank horse stare is "vigilance," actually.
The sheer amount of raw red berries these fierce omnivores consume gives them their distinctive eye color.
The difference between a smile and a grin is the difference between a kiss and tasting.
Glowmites are well-known in the Ringing Deeps for making surprisingly sturdy mounts. This specimen produces a soft cyan glow that kobolds find especially relaxing.
These flying creatures thunder unseen across the heavens. How fortunate that this one has shown itself to you!
Can a wolf's hunger ever be satiated? These lupine brutes seek and devour the enemies of the Horde.
Often roosting along the steep cliff faces of Thaldraszus, they're swift to the skies in times of danger.
A jumble of talons and claws that can fly and swim. No one is safe.
The nice thing is that when they attack, blood almost never stains their feathers. -Mei Francis
Filling the skies of Harandar with a striking pink hue, the Vibrant Petalwing attained its noteworthy pigment through the nectar of various flora it consumes.

After the Sepulcher of the First Ones was opened, this construct of the First Ones was stolen by the brokers and sold to the ethereals in a transaction at the Veiled Market. Under the ethereals' ingenious modifications, it integrated the mysteries of the Aether, gliding through the air with extraordinary elegance, leaving behind a trail of shimmering stardust.
Blackhand is said to have personally designed the fiery armaments used on the Iron Horde's clefthoof battle mounts.
The most wicked and cruel of her kin, Bahmethra endured the full measure of the Banished One's punishments before her fall.
Sporting superb engineering craftsmanship, this chopper is one of the few personal vehicles on Azeroth built for two.
Best keep those bones to yourself if you don't want them crushed.
The Spring Harvesthog is at its most energetic in the early morning. It will spend most of its day snuffling for food or bellowing out calls for other harvesthogs.
With anima once again flowing to the Eternal Forge in Bastion, the plans for the aquilon centurion could be crafted once more.
These magical creatures thrive on love and friendship.
Careful not to consume the ammunition.
The turbulent void magics that have gripped the Sunwell are attracting the rare great manawyrms, corrupting them as they feed on the unbound magics.
This sporeglider derived its striking hue from the unique fungus growing around Teldrassil's roots.
This beautiful basilisk is often hunted for the magical properties of its organs. Fortunately for the basilisk, its connection to ley lines gives it a prescient sense of approaching predators.
The rays of the great sea can travel for many miles in great migratory patterns.

Bred from the fiercest stock anywhere and guaranteed not to bite (much).

Giant crabs are native to Nazjatar and a favored food of the naga. This one must have been well-kept to grow this large.

Armored to withstand collisions in battle.

Wisdom throughout the ages has led to a well-known saying, "Nothing can outrun a cannon."

These fierce beasts are entombed alongside kings so they may carry their masters through the afterlife.

You raised this thing from a scaly pup - Mor'vek would be so proud. But he'd still make you clean up the mess it made in the corner.
The threads are so thin and well-stitched, you can't imagine it wasn't made by magic, strand by strand.

The purebred royal raptors of Zul'Gurub, these mounts have become a rare sight in Stranglethorn Vale. The Gurubashi have been known to fly into a rage at the sight of any non-troll riding one of their precious beasts.

Born from the magma, its carapace was originally molten blobs cooled to form dark-colored volcanic rock. Being imbued by shadowflame has only solidified its unbreakable nature.

Captured from the desolate sands of Vol'dun, this mount is surprisingly docile in captivity.

The Pandaren believe that merely rubbing one's hands on the shiny hide of the ox will grant prosperity, the challenge is catching it.

The flayedwings of Maldraxxus are prized for their ability to soar effortlessly through the skies of the Shadowlands, allowing their rider a surprise opportunity to strike at their foes or support their allies.
Goblin Shredders have proven time and again to be useful in many applications, such as in logging and transportation. This model has been repurposed for use by S.C.R.A.P..
Enigmatic and aloof, this construct of the First Ones flies on a graceful stream of perfect geometric understanding.
At home on the narrow, icy trails of the Storm Peaks, these mammoths are the only mounts the ice giants trust to carry large loads and multiple riders.
Years of chain-chugging potions in Dalaran's sewer system have allowed him to grow large, agile, and shadow resistant.
Give me all the engines you got. - Engineer Cogspinner
The Barak Tor'ol ram's thick bony skull and massive horns make it the ideal mount for charging through groups of armored enemies.
Such a good boy. Or girl. It's hard to tell sometimes. Always good though.
The Storm Peaks! There we will find the beast strong enough to bear me into battle. -Skadi the Ruthless
Formed from the tormented bodies and souls of fallen members of the Army of the Light, the Ur'zul is both fascinating and horrifying.
The check engine light is always on, it's when it goes off that you should be worried.
After diligent training from riders in both worgen and human forms, these horses will now bear any rider in Gilnean finery.
Imagine being so engrossed by a dream that it feels real; some might even call it a delusion.

Arachnid husbandry is a time-honored tradition amongst the Heritage Forces. Though most specimens are used for transport labor or raised to serve as shock troops, the finest examples of their brood are occasionally trained as parade mounts.
The Violet Phoenix's plumage is said to symbolize a union of opposing forces.
Bred by the Revendreth prince, Renathal, these rare dredwing are fiercely loyal and will only let those deemed worthy by the prince himself to interact with them.
These shardhides find it easy to hide in the underbrush, and it is rare to find one that is tamed.
What do you mean is it dyed? Oh, the bird. We did touch up the red just a little. -Trellis Morningsun
Mana rays can emit a bright glow to lure in prey.
This majestic hippogryph hails from the Frayfeather Highlands of Feralas. Though it previously protected its hatchlings, now it chooses to serve a greater cause.

Of all the giants who dared defy the Jailer, Nilganihmaht was the most arrogant. For this transgression, the giant's severed hand was hidden within a veil of torments, and the rings that could summon it back were scattered across the Maw.
Some ottuks get into the spirit of carrying people around more than others.
This tall bird is one of the most graceful and elegant cranes, slightly moreso than the Bronze Crane but less than the Golden Crane.
Ever since acquiring this mount, you have been plagued by strange fever dreams of hippety-hoppety clippety-cloppety elekk on parade.
The Undying Darkhound's parts have graced many battlefields, yet this latest battle may have been the first time they all fought together.
The wood and foliage growing atop this toad is a natural part of its body, helping it siphon anima from the air to nourish itself.
A mighty wolf of Draenor, touched by the fel energies unleashed by Gul'dan in Tanaan Jungle. It has not gone completely mad... yet.
Looking at these majestic creatures, it's not difficult to see how the idea of cervids developed into the stags found on Azeroth and other mortal worlds.
The Horde had dragons, we had the gryphons. We won that war. - Ilsa Blusterbrew
The Barak Tor'ol ram's thick bony skull and massive horns make it the ideal mount for charging through groups of armored enemies.
Only those that have proven themselves against the combined might of the Ascended will be able to ride this mount.
Through the intensive research in the Void, researchers were able to bring this stormray back to life completely tamed.
Fighting the Burning Legion millennia ago, this valiant drake fell to corruption after its body was infused with raw demonic magic.
Magic in the hands of a genius can do wonderful, miraculous things. Magic in the hands of an idiot can make a giant rooster.
Dark spirits flee before the radiance of its presence.
Carve through the night on this loyal, stalwart steed.
This creature was not designed by the First Ones, but instead by an unknown being attempting to create a very fast runner. Needless to say the attempt failed, because this mount is very slow.
The child of Xuen, Ban-Lu has served each Grandmaster faithfully for many years.
The joys of Noblegarden are best when celebrated with this loyal, loving, and blandly-colored freak of nature.
The flames of a courser's hooves express their affinity for a particular school of magic.
His skin more hard than brass was found, that sword nor spear could pierce nor wound.
R E S I S T is carved into the seat in crude letters, along with several, more profane things.
Even the dead need a lift every now and then.
Many believe that during their early lives, these wyrms were forced to fight their own kind for the amusement of others. Perhaps that is why they possess a particularly combative temperament.
Finding a litter of nightsaber kittens, a squad of Blackrock Outriders trained them into a formidable pack of deadly mounts.

A dreamsaber strikes quickly from the shadows, capturing small animals and slipping back into darkness without a sound. The lucky few who have seen a feeding dreamsaber can see them revel in lazily toying with their prey before beginning their meal.
One mon's trash be another mon's loa! Hek hek hek...
The shadeleaf runestag are bred for their ferocity as well as their beauty by the Wild Hunt. They feel no fear charging into the den of any predator.
Their plumage is more beautiful than any other. Subtlety is for the birds! I mean... other birds. -Viera Sunwhisper
These tarachnids move with a purpose unknown to others, answering only to a higher calling. Whatever that may be, it appears to include routine assistance to mortals who need a ride. For now.
Bred from the same vicious line of raptors which sired Ohgan and brought victory to the Gurubashi Empire.
Only the mightiest of heroes ride into battle atop this monstrosity borne of fel and undeath.
Despite their docile nature, talbuks have been known to gore seasoned warriors to death when threatened.
The preferred transportation of the Fenlow family (especially during Hallow's End).
There's nothing more beautiful than watching your imagination take flight.
Talbuks, native to Argus, have evolved chitinous plates to survive the decades of ceaseless war that ravages the landscape.
Teatufts are known for their aromatic teas. However, their playful nature can result in an excess of spilled tea.
Big heart, big dreams, Big Slick.
With anima once again flowing in Sinfall, the Stonewright has been able to infuse these Stoneborn, making them valuable allies in the battles to come.
The Path of Ascension is a challenging trial, and those that display all of the facets the Kyrian hold dear will be duly rewarded.
For so long, the very embodiment of the clouds laid trapped atop a mountain of lightning. And at last, I can feel the wind at my back once again.
Who would have guessed that a shadow elemental would make for such a comfortable ride?
Preserved for thousands of years in stone, bronze magic has nearly aged this mammoth back into a fossil.
The plumage of the Crimson Phoenix is said to represent prosperity and happiness.
The kodo is the backbone of our people. Wherever the Horde goes - in trade, settlement, or war - there you will find the mighty kodo. - Harb Clawhoof
This savage turtle sees red at every turn. Though slow in speed, it is vital to remember that nothing can outrun a cannon.

The first Steel Horde soldiers crossing the Dark Portal captured a ferocious nightsaber. Blackrock artisans armed it with magma armor, transforming it into a combat weapon. Warriors may customize its parts at the Morphing Forum to suit their fighting style and dominate the battlefield.
There is an old Zandalari saying about wild direhorns: "Run!"
Relax. The future will unfold as it was meant to, one way or an otter.
While it's not exactly common, the representatives of the Severed Threads assure you that swarmites are more than capable of carrying your weight if you choose to ride it.

The instability of primalist storms in potential timelines sometimes causes creatures to absorb the energies from the very storms. These creatures tend to be docile towards those who are able to face the fury of these chronomatic anomalies.
Its breath is worse than its bite.
The long talons of the velocidrake give it an edge on the plains.
The terradynamic exo-plotters are conjoined by hydraulic imaging to the equilibrium enhancers... -Binjy Featherwhistle
These beautiful helicids emerge only at night. When they are pleased, their shells hum with a joyful melody.
According to Wildhammer legend, the orange plumage found on gryphons is believed to be a hereditary trait passed down from their elemental ancestry.

When you're ready for fun you're ready for the Fantastical Goblin Waveshredder. Guaranteed to bring the fun.



*Disclaimer: Fun not guaranteed
Forged by human, gnome, and dwarf, this armored masterpiece is designed to slice a tauren into a tri-tip dinner with a flick of the handlebars.
The Forsaken believe that without a purpose, even beasts of burden suffer in undeath.
Ensuring there is always some marginal distance between you and rock bottom.
Twice as acid-filled as the usual fiend.
Pried from a giant Hearthstone game box.
Male rams will often smash their thick skulls against each other for hours to impress a female. In that way, they're very similar to dwarves.
Born in the mountains of Stormheim, this terrifying fusion of storm and scale sets the sky ablaze in pursuit of its prey.
If he wasn't so full, you wouldn't have caught him.
It's trained to survive the harsh climate of Frostfire Ridge, so it snuggles as if its life depended on it.
When you absolutely, positively have to be there right now. -Rillie Spindlenut
After the fall of the Bastion of Twilight, a few scattered twilight whelps escaped Vexiona's sway. Some of these whelps have allied with mortals and are willing to bear them as riders.
The prized possession of Haymar the devout. Unclear if he would be anything if not for his epic void bike. Formerly assigned to patrolling the streets of Stormwind after its fall.
A few of the Argent Crusade's swiftest mounts were awarded to those members of the Alliance who performed exceptionally during the tournament in Icecrown.
Steadfast and proud, this steed carries its rider with quiet dignity and unyielding resolve.
Even the dead need a lift every now and then.
A dragonhawk whose wings shine as brightly as the leaves of its Eversong home.
Perfect for the up-and-comer who wants to climb the ladder by making everyone else's business THEIR business.
Heroes who proved their might in the gladiatorial arenas during the Cataclysm were awarded the most exceptional of the twilight drake broods.
One of the last of the giant bats to escape Undercity following the siege of Lordaeron.
A compilation of nuts, bolts, gears, and treated wood paneling make for an unusually speedy ride.
From the foothills of Khaz Modan, we followed its ember-lit wings--a northbound torch across the dark summer sky. - The Pilgrimage of the First Wildsage
Only a few gryphons are selected to be Sea Scouts operating from flag ships in the fleet. Their long range reconnaissance is an integral part of Kul Tiran sea dominance.
The vrykul were the first to recognize their potential. Or maybe the second, depending on how you look at it.
The majestic crane is a treasured friend of the pandaren.
Ancient mounts of the Highborne, now left to run wild in the Broken Isles, they can rarely be found due to their latent magical powers.

In the corners of Azeroth, stories are told of a dreaded dragon who swept a pall of torment over the land. In some versions of this story, his fiery presence brought cataclysmic death and destruction worldwide. In other versions, he is blue.

Whispers tell of the Giganto Manis, a titanic creature said to dwell within Azeroth's very veins. Those who claim to have seen it speak of claws vast enough to pierce a dragon's heart, and sharp enough to carve through the finest armor forged by mortal hands.
From their infancy, Thundering Cloud Serpents are drawn to storms. They have been known to chase lightning through the blackened, roiling clouds, and to bathe in the pouring rain.
This snail protects its treasures with the ferocity of a dragon, but perhaps not the speed.
Always moving forward to position yourself above the pawns below.
The necrorays of Maldraxxus prefer to congregate around the enormous decaying mushrooms of the region.
While most salamanthers' attention jumps freely from one attraction to the next, this one enjoys long periods of deep observation.

Once the loyal mount of a House Briarbane lord, it turned on the lord and his retinue. Members of House Briarbane now whisper of a dark Gargon lying in wait even baiting venthyr who venture through the darker parts of the Chalice District of Revendreth.
The orcs once hunted these graceful herd animals as part of the om'riggor rite of passage ceremony.
Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night stays these charming couriers from the swift completion of their appointed rounds.
The spirit of the Great Hunter found you worthy, and now its children will answer your call forevermore.
A gift from the Ohn'ir, these ohuna are invaluable companions when scouting new horizons for the Dragonscale Expedition.
In ages past, the sun rocs of Kalimdor were believed to be the messengers of An'she, carrying with them the first flame before dawn and the final light of evenfall.
Born, bred and battle tested in Gilneas.
The wolves of the Horde are befriended, not domesticated.
The kodo is the backbone of our people. Wherever the Horde goes - in trade, settlement, or war - there you will find the mighty kodo. - Harb Clawhoof
Little is known about the origination of phalynx technology, the machinations of which are taught more akin to religion than engineering.
Prized by horse breeders for their discipline and steadfastness.
Once a pack member dies, these shredclaws enter a frenzy of rage that not even a hulking ultradon can stop.
One of the heartiest of species that inhabit the slopes of Highmountain, they can survive for months in freezing blizzards.
Brewers retired this mount from active advertising service after complaints that the beasts were "too temperamental" to control in major cities.
One of many such mechsuits designed to guard the Machine. After years of faithful service it is no longer suited for combat. It does make for an impressive conveyance, though.
When one cosmically invasive threat meets another, sometimes the smaller will end up on the menu of the larger. At least cosmic observers don't always chew their meals.
Assuring others that your assets are exactly where they should be.
Dead or alive, you're coming with me.
After being freed from vicious harpies by Cairne and Thrall, many of these creatures became valuable companions of the Horde.
The kind nature of alpacas makes them perfect as companions for the intrepid adventurer.
The Summer Harvesthog enjoys laying out in the sun or going for a swim in a clear lake. They are excellent at foraging for food, but need to be coaxed into it.
No one quite knows when the legend of Grumpus began in Draenor, but his toys are just the worst.
Brood of Karokta, raised in the underlight of Zaralek Cavern.
Sturdy and steady; "the horse that built Stormwind."
The first instance of a flaming shalewing ever discovered. Nine out of ten researchers agree: it's hot!
Wildhammer Fact Checker claims that this specific breed was the first type of ram domesticated by the dwarves when they settled in Dun Morogh.
Take to the sky on the most loyal and loving fox on Azeroth.
The chess event was not to be contained. So Medivh fashioned this conveyance to take it on trips.
Due to their preference for dark caves and murky waters, sightings of this unique breed of salamanther are so rare that many researchers thought they had gone extinct.
It's not world-devouringly bad, just misunderstood.
One has not truly lived until they have felt the tidal current rushing through their hair while atop a majestic seahorse, said no one.  Ever.
Take to the skies on a glittering, shimmering, spring butterfly.
When Kyparite is depleted of its amber essence it becomes fairly resistant to the corrosion from rocket fuel.
Dreamrunners flit between this world and the Emerald Dream at will, reveling in their wild nature.
A creature blessed by the wilds, it moves with the steadfast spirit and gentle strength the Amani hold sacred.
The Kul Tiran military prides itself on mastery of both sea, through a vast navy, and land, with armed cavalry.
Loyal hounds of the Curator, these gargon patrol the crypts and catacombs deterring both trespassing and escape.
The Forsaken believe that without a purpose, even beasts of burden suffer in undeath.
The eternal twilight of the Underrot has robbed this crawg of all pigmentation.

The plants of the deep lands often emulate the creatures of of Azeroth. The purpose of the mimicry is unknown, but can be quite disturbing when the terrestrial mollusks are on the wrong end of an arboreal meal.
Soaring high above the Battle of Dazar'alor, these beasts are drawn to the most cunning of victors.
Only the swiftest heroes venturing into the troll temple of Zul'Aman were able to subdue these rare battle mounts.
This mischievous drake enjoys flying through geysers and volcanic plumes.
The wolves of the Horde are befriended, not domesticated.
Bearing Zul'Aman's fiercest riders, its shadowed wings strike down any who dare resist.
Each step echoes with the rage of your three opponents.
The shattering of Argus caused the mana rays to mutate and adapt to their surroundings. Some of them abandoned their pigments in favor of strengthening their senses.
Well-suited for compacting trash into rollable balls. Junkmaestro apocrypha claims these might become worlds of their own if only they could get big enough.
Comes from a lineage of fine horses that once grazed near the shores of the Well of Eternity.
They say that proto-drakes can smell fear. This iron-bound monster FEEDS off of it.
Only a handful of these giant bats remain in the Arathi Highlands, carefully raised by the Witherbark forest trolls who first brought them here.
Harnessing the elemental powers of the storm, these majestic beasts crackle like lightning and roar like thunder.
A very rare Korthian creature, due to limited cloud cover.
Rescued from the ruthless charge of Ol' Waxbeard and the looming threat of The Darkness, now able to nibble on loose wax in peace.
These mighty leapers have adapted to island life by learning to catch seagulls swooping through crags and fissures.

Surface-dwelling children often profess desires for a pony or wolf of their own upon reaching certain milestones of age. A young Widow Arak'nai had similar ambitions, though her tastes would likely be considered eclectic by some standards.
Cherished for their heavy carrying capacity and steady gait, these stalwart beasts are the mount of choice for most native Pandaren.
I cannot help but wonder if things would have turned out different if the titans had elevated even one more dragonflight. -Alexstrasza
Cautious by direwolf standards, the dustmane can only be coaxed to ride with something it considers special.
Destined to become queen of her hive, she scouts Kul Tiras and Zandalar in search of a suitable home for a new colony to flourish.

Whatever the purpose of these cervids once was, it is long forgotten. Though they are not Dominated, they have been corrupted by the unintended presence of Mawsworn in the sacred realm of Zereth Mortis.
Nether Rays are among the most trusted, versatile mounts in all of Outland and beyond.
Three elements have been fused to create this magical disc, which is attuned to your specific magical powers.
One of the bold equines of the Broken Isles, unmatched among the steeds of Azeroth in ferocity and strength.
One-time companion of Kanga the Primal, the fallen troll hero. The raptor's name is unknown, for Kanga only spoke to it in bear form.
I thought the thing was ill until it took to the air. It flies as true as any of my own. -Alexstrasza

An early eternal traveler encountered the furline and befriended a pair. Accompanying the traveler back to their domain, these furline kittens were forever changed by living there and accompanying the travelers.
The patterns on the wings of that creature resemble sand flowing through an hourglass. One could gaze upon them for ages...
This fel-infused feathered friend flaps its wings at a frenetic pace to remain far above the frenzy below.
It takes a great deal of effort to decorate a corpsefly, but some would say the efforts are worth it.

The plants of the deep lands often emulate the creatures of of Azeroth. The purpose of the mimicry is unknown, but can be quite disturbing when the terrestrial mollusks are on the wrong end of an arboreal meal.
The results of a fel infusion experiment with one of Skorpyron's offspring.
A gift from Granpap Whiskers to the Trading Post, amber skitterflies are remarkably docile.
A veteran of some of the toughest battles fought by the Argent Crusade.
The gargon are the loyal mounts and companions of the Venthyr and Renathal has found many abandoned at Sinfall, awaiting reawakening and assignment to worthy members of the covenant.
Night elves once believed that seeing this light colored saber breed in the wild was an ill omen.
Be it into the flood, or into the fire, this one will go where you require.
These creatures are found sneaking through the battlefield and climbing over obstactles, ready to cause trouble for the Alliance.
Its rider died during battle, and so the saddle is passed to you.
Bloodbathed Vanquishers are so named when it is determined that a reanimated frost wyrm died a particularly gruesome and bloody death.
The fur of this Windsteed is not only colored to match its woodland home, but also usually contains bits of bark and leaves.
When fallen heroes are raised into undeath, so too are their horses.
The connection between a nightsaber and its hunter or huntress is nearly inseparable.
The residents of Pandaria salute your enthusiasm for wildlife preservation. They do have concerns about housing 150 animals per visit, though.
Although Ji-Kun feasted on the failed creations of mogu flesh-shapers, her progeny is willing to eat more pedestrian carcasses.
These brilliantly colored cloud serpents have scales that are a mixture of ruby, gold, and nearly violet.
As lighthearted and gentle as the snow, they can bounce from one snowdrift to the next without leaving a print.
Introduced as an invasive species to K'aresh, Krolusk have found some use as beasts of burden.
Victory is not a simple matter of strength, but having the wisdom and ability to deliver the strength where it is needed most.
A symbol of vengeance throughout all known realms.

The treachery of Hrestimorak was infamous, betraying his people to claim power. Facing damnation in the Maw, he tried to subvert the Jailer... a foolish act that would earn him an eternity of torment.
Red-colored vombata are considered lucky by the Enlightened. It was a red vombata that was present when they first arrived in Zereth Mortis.
As anima flows to the distant wealds of Ardenweald once more, the wilderlings awaken and cautiously emerge from their canopy burrows.
This sporeglider likes to gently nuzzle its riders.
Awarded to only the most skilled champions from the Trial of the Crusader, these steeds were chosen for Horde members from Tirion Fordring's own personal stable.
A favorite unit of the Lich King, both for its power as a siege weapon, and the satisfying sound of flung meat.
At daybreak, the noble Sunwalkers often perform rituals to bless their mounts, imbuing them with holy magic.
Filled with the hatred of an ancient god, the dread raven are the Arakkoa's most trusted guardians.
The Horde had dragons, we had the gryphons. We won that war. - Ilsa Blusterbrew

Some helicids of Zereth Mortis have strangely metallic shells. The ones who do are generally a bronze color, indistinct from the metal any novice miner could work, save that this creature's construction far surpasses the skill of any novice.
Wilderlings serve as support units in battle, preserving their allies and rendering enemy magics useless.
After the unburdened Emperor Shaohao gave his final breath to protect his people, a golden serpent descended from the heavens to alight the emperor's spirit to the peaks of Kun-Lai Summit.
The moods of these tempestuous mounts are known to shift as unpredictably and as violently as their physical forms.
These giant seahorses are naturally curious, and are often found exploring sunken ship wreckage for shiny things.
One of Darmac's trained beasts, its tusks can pierce even the hardest Iron Horde steel.
Some of the natural wildlife of Argus, like the mana ray, has survived and adapted to life on the shattered world.
To be the Lord of the Corpseflies, you've got to lay a LOT of eggs.
Packaged upgrades include; dual-lantern fog lights, emergency brew keg, and genuine Tanji leather seat.  - Turtlemaster Odai
When waking a tiger, use a long stick. Better yet, tell your friend to wake the tiger instead. -Pandaren Proverb
Qinsho wrought his eternal guardian from pure gold and imbued it with the resilience of the earth.
Despite their mischievous and playful nature, these creatures make for loyal and dependable travelling companions.
As the isles awaken, these proto-drakes answer the call to soar the skies alongside mortals.
Born and raised during a time of great chaos, this mount has survived hardships known by few.
Created by a mogu sorcerer who breathed life into their favorite pet rock.
The Gloombough not only have uniquely dark coloring, but are entirely nocturnal, making them one of the rarest tree-dwellers to spot in person.
Packaged upgrades include; dual-lantern fog lights, emergency brew keg, and genuine Tanji leather seat.  - Turtlemaster Odai
But the most important rule, the rule you can never forget, no matter how much he cries, no matter how much he begs, never feed him after midnight.
Slow and steady might not always win you the race but it'll get you there... eventually.
The most aggressive nether drakes were awarded those heroes who showed significant prowess and commitment in the gladiatorial arena.
The shattering of Argus drove this breed of mana ray to bloodthirst. It now subsists on the corrupted blood of any creatures it can sink its many teeth into.
Formed by Ragnaros himself as a gift for the daughter he never had.

An artist in the magical city of Dalaran fell asleep on her brush, and dreamed of painting a beautiful feathered dragon. Her artwork leapt from the page, and when she awoke, she found it sleeping gently beside her.
The garn are the most fierce predators on Draenor, and always hunt in packs.
The Pterrordax could and would eat you in seconds. Are you sure sitting on its back is a good idea?
This animal's color mimics the clear blue of Draenor's river shallows, making it almost invisible to aquatic predators.
The seldom seen native of the Azure Span is considered blessed by the tuskaar of the region.
Legends say that an ancient pandaren emperor crafted the first jeweled panther for his son after the boy's twin brother died of an illness.
A brilliant-plumed hawkstrider that escaped from the Silvermoon stables, who knows where in Eversong it may be hiding?
This grimlynx has seen many battles against the creatures in the Rift of Aln.
The razor-thin wings of this scarab are well-protected by a gleaming, yet indestructible jade-carved carapace.
Fire can transform stone in exciting ways, but never let the Stonemother know I said that. -Earthcaller Yevaa
Little is known about this elusive species of ray, found only in the dark waters surrounding Darkmoon Island.
These dreamsabers are ferocious in battle, yet lethargic and often found lazily outstretched upon open fields. After soaking in the warmth of daylight, their flame flares that much brighter.
Frequently used by kobolds as mounts, the Assembly of the Deeps has decided to allow you access to one of their most loyal mudnoses.
What it lacks in safety features it more than makes up for in speed and style.  Not for the faint of heart.
Is the emerald drake rare?  You have no idea.  If I had a silver for every time someone asked me about one, I could have retired years ago. -Mei Francis
Forced to recall the model after numerous complaints of an "uncontrollable throttle", Gnomish engineers now refer to a proto-type blunder as a "model B".
Keeps the peace by turning you into pieces.
These exceptionally agile fliers make excellent mounts once they've been trained not to sap every ounce of anima from their rider.
Intended for the most devoted of the Sureki elite, these skyrazors were favored by Queen Ansurek for both their cunning and brutality.
Spriggan riders tie bits of anima-less detritus to the end of sticks in front of their gorm mounts to steer. It's... an imperfect art.
A vile ritual can give the ritual master great power. It can also give the target of the ritual great power. This can sometimes go well or poorly for the ritual master.
Fennimore Quigley is credited with milking the first camel and breaking the record for "longest unintentional flight," all in the same afternoon.
The strange icy flames cause you to sweat and shiver at the same time.
Legends tell of a spell placed upon a hunting raptor who dared to snarl at young Tyrande Whisperwind as she bathed in a jungle pool. The beast is cursed to wander Azeroth -  until it apologizes.
Nerissa trampled over countless bodies on the back of Gorespine as she rose to prominence as the commander of the Lichsworn forces for the House of Rituals.
This soul eater's gaze unnerves you. Best not meet its eyes for too long.
Born in the mountains of Stormheim, this terrifying fusion of storm and scale sets the sky ablaze in pursuit of its prey.
Corrupted by demonic power and once forced to serve the Shadow Council.
This ancient mogu artifact controls ambient fog to enable levitation.
He emerges from the water, fins swaying lazily in the breeze, sun-kissed scales glittering. He is... Fabious.
The Crest-Horn will often be drawn to graze on the plants that grow in the sea. Some have braved the fiercest wildlife there, making them true Kalu'ak.
Wyverns hail from some of the most inhospitable regions of Kalimdor, making them masters of adapting to any environment.
When Quan the Relentless fell in battle, his loyal hounds waited for his return. Millenia later, they remain patient.
Jepetto may have over done it a little...
The turbo trike's tri-wheel design adds superior stability and a smaller turn radius over its two wheeled cousins.
Integrated into the depleted forces of the Wild Hunt, the fawn riders quickly found that the gorm's powerful mandibles were perfect for cutting down close enemy ranks.
The orcs once hunted these graceful herd animals as part of the om'riggor rite of passage ceremony.
Surging with the kind of energy and enthusiasm that can make anyone envious.
Scarred by the chaos wrought by decades of conflict, this fel-infused steed is a perfect match for an intrepid adventurer.
A remnant of the Black Empire's past, these precursors of the abyss worms are once again resurging with the rise of Ny'alotha.
The Palehide Mushan is the tastiest of Mushan beasts, but it hates being reminded of that fact.
He's big, he's ready for battle, and he's a bear. What more could you want in a mount?
Created by deciphering and performing powerful runic magic, this Shadehound is bound to its creator.
For a brief time, many orcs would declare themselves "hungry like an Orgrimmar wolf." Some blood elves still use the phrase ironically.
A good warhorse is loyal to its bones. Having shed its mortal coil, this steed is an omen of eternal strife.
With fur to match the deep roots and armor to match the vast foliage, these Grimlynx are equipped to be some of the ultimate hunters of Harandar.
Radiating warmth and grace, it soars on wings of light.
Talbuks, native to Argus, have evolved chitinous plates to survive the decades of ceaseless war that ravages the landscape.
Don't be deceived by its bright colors, it is capable of sneaking up on anyone (or anything).
Only rewarded to those who have bested their foes in battle.
One can't help but think what it might feel like to pluck the stars from their fixture in the sky. Perhaps, Stargrazer will show us how someday.

Not all of Medivh's victims are gone for good.
Woven together by some of the grumpiest Dalaran mages, this flying quilt is known for its comfort and fluffy pillows.
An ancient mogu artifact awarded to those who are deeply committed to the skies.
Long ago, the dusk-painted silhouettes of these sun rocs inspired many fireside myths. Their return to Kalimdor has reignited lost stories of these heralds of An'she.
It has an armored spike on its tail. Scratch its belly at your own risk.
Cherished for their heavy carrying capacity and steady gait, these stalwart beasts are the mount of choice for most native Pandaren.
When it comes to taming devourers, all it takes is a little anima and a lot of patience. And a lot of healing potions.

The snowpaw inhabit the frigid afterlives of the Shadowlands, reveling in their frosty environment. Travelers thought lost to the deadly blizzards of Northrend would sometimes miraculously be found alive, proclaiming that they owe their lives to the mysterious foxes that protected them.
Accidentally transported when the Brokers moved Tazavesh, this gorger has found a new world ripe with potential sources of energy, such as anima beacons...and riders.
The magnificent August Phoenixes are blessed by Chi-Ji to fill the hearts of riders with wonder and hope for the future.

Tricks have been played, your enemies beaten, this ghoulish charger awaits a treat, friend.

The rivers of Pandaria, like Wen Lo, are unpredictable in nature. They may remain calm, bringing water to the crops, or flood, bringing ruin. Wen Lo reminds us that we must adapt to the challenges of life.

It is a sad fact that even the wise and majestic hippogryph may fall prey to corruption.
Cormaera were an early species on Azeroth that were claimed by elemental lords.
This shredder has been lovingly painted with a non-corrosive paint to ensure a lasting sheen.

The yellow ottuks of the Azure Span are sleek, sneaky, and smart. Those trained for war are the finest tuskarr cavalry mounts, equally capable on the ground and in the waters.
Whatever dark magic once compelled the Twilight Harbinger is now broken... or is it?
The spikes on this beast can pierce plate armor with ease -- only the most elite riders can even consider mounting this deadly pincushion.
Raised in the Alterac Mountains by the Frostwolf Clan, trained to bite dwarves.
Draped in tattered circus banners, this eerie mount is a perfect blend of shadow and spectacle.
You don't get dogs hotter than this.
In the darkened skies of Revendreth, you cannot see these creatures coming until it is too late.
A gift from Merithra, who blessed these thunderspines to ensure that no matter where the Maruuk clans roam, they will always be under the green dragonflight's protection.

Most vombata enjoy tunneling through the ground, but these sniffers seem to have an unerring ability to locate crystals buried deep underground and will congregate around large deposits.

Said to be leaner and potentially even meaner than the venerable Bruce. Bruno's legacy is yet to be written.

Twisted by the void, these winged creatures now rule the skies of K'aresh.

Looking into the eyes of this mystical beast is like peering into the heart of the sun. Goggles are recommended when you're riding.
A curious and inquisitive doe, she doesn't mean to worry her master, she just gets distracted easily. Especially with all of the new things to see on Korthia.
This species of ray seems to have evolved to stalk its prey amidst the brightly colored corals of the seas.

I still don't get why they fly faster when you put armor on them. -Drakma

Garishly sporting extreme amounts of goblin flair, Gallywix commissioned his Mech of Death to one up Mekkatorque in combat and more importantly in style.

Likely stolen from Newstead in the Arathi Highlands, this stalwart little donkey was destined to be eaten by kobolds.

This aircraft will help you delve straight into adventure, or maybe other dimensions!
The phalynx does not fetch, though it is not known why this is.
Some within the Ascended keep a phalynx as a pet. While they may not be as furry as a larion, they are much less likely to eat your other pets.
When Korthia was pulled into The Maw, only a few hardy species survived.
Kaldorei legends whisper of a relentless hunter prowling amongst the deepest shadows of Kalimdor, never sleeping. By the light of the sun or the moon, Ash'adar now hunts with you.
Unseen for many years, this brightly hued hawkstrider emerged from hiding to help defend the Ghostlands from the Scourge. Its prowess shines as brilliantly as its feathers.
Night elves raise frostsaber cubs from infancy, forging lifelong bonds of trust between rider and beast.
For when you're making a crash landing in the middle of an uncharted swamp because it's the only way to access that ancient temple.

A favorite of warriors of the Exodar.
Sha has warped this tiger into an even more fearsome creature. The emotions that flow through this creature make it an unmistakable harbinger of doom.

The moths of Ardenweald play a vital role in the ecosystem, carrying spores, anima, and pollen from one part of the forest to the other, providing nourishment and variation to the denizens living below.

Bred from the fiercest stock anywhere and guaranteed not to bite (much).

Circling above the dying and the doomed, its wings herald plague, ruin, and the certainty that nothing left in its shadow will rise again.
After promising to fly you to the ends of Outland, the netherwing drake was eventually drawn to the blue skies of Azeroth as well.
Buzzing through the time punctual as ever, these Buzzbees harvest the errant sands of time and return them safely to the Timeways.
At Warchief Hellscream's command, Horde trainers began raising wolves to thrive in the shock and ferocity of sustained combat.
A nightmarish steed of hardened steel and vengeful spirits, this companion will follow you to the depths of the Firelands and back without complaint.
An ancient mogu artifact awarded to those who are deeply committed to forms of currency.
Its ethereal spirit is barely contained by its iron shell. The penultimate creation of Salanar the Horseman, these powerful steeds were once thought to have all been destroyed.

First designed as a booster for a much larger rocket, the X-51 was determined to give the perfect thrust capacity for a single rider payload.
Necrorays lay their eggs in small clusters within the frills and hollows of decaying fungal blooms.

These cloud serpents have scales that... are the color of clouds, actually.

Bred specifically to honor those heroes who showed exceptional resilience and fortitude facing the dangers in Northrend.

Finding a litter of nightsaber kittens, a squad of Kor'kron Outriders trained them into a formidable pack of deadly mounts.

Wandering the glades of Felwood on a steady diet of cursed truffles and lost travelers. Do not pet.

Riding this mount fills you with a stillness and peace that is not frequently known to accompany murlocs or bears.

A fiercely intelligent and curious species, these fox-like creatures have travelled the Great Dark Beyond and found their way to Azeroth. Drawn to Azeroth's champions, they seek adventure and companionship.

A shadeleaf runestag is capable of goring creatures as powerful as a gorm matriarch in defense of its herd. The Wild Hunt ride these mounts into dangerous corners of the Shadowlands, when their domain must be defended from those who would threaten the wilds.
Bug spray and a hat with netting aren't going to do much in the swamps of Nazmir, bring a club.

Only the richest cartel leaders are able to afford the metals required to craft the Cartel Master's Gearglider.

The best mount, logically, serves multiple purposes -- sometimes you need to get places AND reach something high up once you get there.

The tauralus that serve the armies of Maldraxxus have had all traits of compassion bred out of them, and are only adorned in armor when they show that no sword or spell can stop them from carrying their rider to victory.
Forged from the sins of countless diabolical dungeon denizens. Only those with the skills to overcome them may hold its reins.
The soldiers of Maldraxxus protect the Shadowlands, and require a mount that is both capable and calm when faced with overwhelming odds.
Can howl loudly enough to be heard for miles.
Sandstone Drakes were studied in great detail long ago by the famed alchemist Walleye Sprysprocket. It has even been said that Walleye developed potions to mimic the drakes' physiology.

A shalewing born in the wake of Fyrakk's destructive breach. Cursed by his primal flame, its temperature slowly but constantly rises. It must immerse itself in water to cool off periodically, lest its own heat smother it.
The tauralus has two tails, which are both absolutely necessary for whipping away buzzing pests like the bloodlouse.
Legends say that an ancient pandaren emperor crafted the first jeweled panther for his son after the boy's twin brother died of an illness.
Longtime allies of the trolls, these jungle hunters form a special bond with their masters. They become mount, guardian, and friend.
This Slateback got lost wandering into various phases as it followed some ethereals around.
Sworn defender of the Elven people, animated by arcane power and an unyielding will to protect.

King Mechagon's private aerial unit, complete with deployable blast cannon and foot warmers.

One of the Arathi horses, taken and broken by the Horde conquerors of Stromgarde.

Armored to withstand collisions in battle.

Some of our brethren prefer horses, but the hawkstrider will always be the true symbol of Silvermoon. -Winaestra
Despite their name, aquamarine basilisks feast on a variety of coastal crystals and oceanic rocks.

When the void energies were released, it drove most windriders feral. They killed each other and their trainers. The gates to their roost were locked by the survivors. Some surviving windriders can still be seen gliding above, but none dare return to their new deadly domain to see what remains.
One of the bold equines of the Broken Isles, unmatched among the steeds of Azeroth in ferocity and strength.
This noble gryphon is as staunch a battle companion as any member of the Alliance could ask for.
Ve'nari has many methods of sneaking around the Maw and disrupting the Jailer's plans, including binding his own minions.

Aggressive and territorial, the mosshide is known for hiding in river-shore scrub and ambushing unwary passersby.

Somehow this grove crawler remains untouched by the horrors that overran Fungara Village.

Tuskaar aren't often found on Highmountain, but the crest-horns often come down to the shores to seek rare delicacies in the coastal waters.

The few of these mysterious creatures that remain appear to be impossibly old, almost timeless. Perhaps they were created by the First Ones, because no schematic to synthesize these has yet been discovered.

A phalynx is considered both a worthy companion and a lithe opponent to test one's reflexes against.
This rare giant crab has taken a break from its nautical nonsense deep under the sea to explore the surface.

A scrupulous breed of prowlers whose ferocity can only be matched by that of the worgen. These decisive creatures embody discipline and a controlled viciousness that even the worgen have come to admire.

A rare variety of the Amani eagle, Sharptalons strike with terrifying precision and fly with unparalleled grace.

One of Al'ar's last clutch, Belo'ren was taken to the Isle of Quel'Danas and raised to defend the Sunwell from any who would threaten it with his very life. It is said that death will never claim him.
Come not between the dragon and his wrath.
The backbone of the Alliance air force is comprised predominantly of gnomish flying machines due to their maneuverability and speed.

Its calm temperament makes it ideal to train young children in horseback riding.
One would think controlling a rampaging mount would be difficult, but if you can learn to control the direction of the rampage it can be quite useful.
Many night elves revere these proud mounts because their shimmering coats symbolize the goddess of the moon, Elune.
A veteran of some of the toughest battles fought by the Argent Crusade.
