Once a simple beetle of the Forbidden Reach, Telix became infused with storm magic when Raszageth was unleashed. With its newly heightened senses, Telix roams the Dragon Isles alongside the Dragonscale Expedition--and you!

The gargon of the Inquisitors are some of the most vicious ever carved. The Avowed seek to recapture these beasts and return them to the righteous duty of assisting in the purifying of souls rather than the perversions performed at the hands of the Inquisitors.
The gnarled horns of this armoredon are far stronger than bone.

Doesn't actually seem like anything too special under the hood, but just wait until those goblins next door see you pull up for the next pool party.

A flurrious, fridgid friend, frost-flecked for frozen fun.
In the void-scarred wake of the All-Devouring and his kith, twisted remnants of distant worlds and forgotten aeons find their way across the Great Dark.
These sleek foxes can prowl amongst newly-fallen leaves without making a sound, even at this size.

Mischievous spriggans and the valerunners have a natural enmity. No valerunner would deign to allow a spriggan rider because they can sense their inherent malevolence. This angers the trickster spriggans who take twisted enjoyment in playing cruel pranks on these majestic creatures.
Silver Covenant Hippogryphs are fiercely loyal, both to their riding partners, and to the Alliance.
Nether Rays are among the most trusted, versatile mounts in all of Outland and beyond.
These icy minions come from an unknown plane far from this one.

Corrupted by the presence of the Dark Star in Draenor, the Voidtalons resisted being broken by the Shadowmoon Clan and were ultimately destroyed by Ner'zhul. Only a single egg remains, lost in the void.
Still one of the most vicious steeds stabled in Karazhan.
Adept at blending into dense, magical forests, such as one may find around the Broken Isles.
Metal once ruined, restored to life by scrap and song.
Even from within her prison, Raszageth's primal scorn brought the mightiest beasts to heel.
The only known Razzashi Raptors were said to have been in the custody of Bloodlord Mandokir in Zul'Gurub.  This species of raptor has not been seen in many years.
Born in the mountains of Stormheim, this terrifying fusion of storm and scale sets the sky ablaze in pursuit of its prey.
Bred for destruction by an insane warlord in a far-off land, but at least the seat is warm.
The forsaken prefer the use of these bloodthirsty hunters, both for their speed as a mount, and the psychological effect they have on their enemies.
A valiant steed on the Arathi Highlands, it knows no fear.
Historians claim that these incorporeal beasts were created when Draenor exploded, unleashing energies that warped the world's flora and fauna.
Both the name and color of this majestic phoenix are believed to symbolize rebirth.
The sky's the limit when you mount up on this "Motion By Emotion" magic broom model.
The Army of the Light conducts quick, brutal hit-and-run attacks using these agile war machines.

The plants of the deep lands often emulate the creatures of of Azeroth. The purpose of the mimicry is unknown, but can be quite disturbing when the terrestrial mollusks are on the wrong end of an arboreal meal.
For years pandaren believed these creatures to be untamable. Just ask the first pandaren to do so, Henshi "Limp Along" Homebrew.
Silas considered using his fleet of blimps for marketing, but decided that selling them directly was all the marketing he needed.
The Witherbark warrior Beastrider Kama once cut bloody swathes of terror across the Arathi Highlands astride such a monster.
These ardenmoths prefer the dark and damp forests of northwest Ardenweald, where fungal colonies are perpetually blooming.
Chiseled by the stonemasons of Stormwind, this stone gryphon symbolizes the unbending courage of the Alliance.
I may question Prince Kael'thas's loyalties, but never his style. -Elrodan
These coursers have long been known to exist, but only befriend those that have gone to great lengths for friendship.
When fallen heroes are raised into undeath, so too are their horses.
These breezestriders' red coloration reflects their temperament: sanguine, fierce, and courageous.
Nether Rays are among the most trusted, versatile mounts in all of Outland and beyond.
Smaks knows a thing or two about caring for hyenas. Rule number one: keep your hands away from those teeth!
Born in the middle of an ice storm, this armoredon prefers its meals partially frozen.
The only thing these big cats bring home as gifts are the severed limbs of your enemies.
Any captain worth their salt knows to have a trustworthy navi-gator.
A technological marvel in the flesh, this K'arroc represents hope for a brighter K'aresh.
These tarachnids make their home in the darkest corners of Zereth Mortis, coming out only to hunt (or, sometimes, carry a rider around).
A beacon of hope; a guiding light in the darkness.

This warbear mother was captured by the Twilight's Blade while protecting her cub. Her continued separation from her cub is only angering her more. Anyone who manages to reunite her with her cub will have her eternal loyalty.
Emerging from the chaos of the early elemental wars on Azeroth, the Coldflame Tempest is a reminder that the chill of a blizzard is eternal.
Normally bugs are for bait, but how could you look into its eyes and even think that? -Nat Pagle
Farewell, Tarecgosa. A dear sister, hero, student, and teacher. Though blood does not bind us, you will always be family. May your soul find its place soaring among the stars.
The last known Zulian tigers were kept by High Priest Thekal, deep within Zul'Gurub.  They are said to have been hunted into extinction.
Common to the dark forests of Drustvar, these gryphon are silent and swift. Their prowess at operating on their own or as mounts lends them to be used for ambush and shock tactics.
I remember my first flying carpet... yeti hair and burlap.  Not nearly as nice as this one here. - Frozo the Renowned
This formidable creature's lineage may be traced to Galakras, and yet further to Galakrond, one of the most infamous of all proto-dragons.
Raised in the Alterac Mountains by the Stormpike Clan, trained to headbutt orcs.
The Qiraji War Tank has only been seen recently during the Call of the Scarab, could this hint at a resurfacing of the deadly creatures?
The Amani trolls ride this fierce creature on ceremonial hunts in honor of the bear god Nalorakk.
Earthen have long used ramoliths as beasts of burden due to their hardy nature. Shale ramoliths are considered to be friendlier than most others, though that isn't saying much.
These playful protectors of the Emerald Dream may be larger than their faerie dragon relatives, but they are no less mischievous.
Speed, cunning, and ferocity are the things trolls and raptors admire about each other.
Fast and dependable, Shredclaws were one of the first creatures tamed in the Voidstorm. Their owners learned quickly not to leave them alone with their pets.
Born and raised during a time of great chaos, this mount has survived hardships known by few.
Its crimes can not be pardoned.
You are Azeroth's true guardians and the future of this world is in your hands, for the dawning of the age of mortals has begun. - Alexstrasza
Like their distant nightsaber cousins, tigers are renowned for their razor-sharp claws, incredible agility, and love of being scratched behind the ears.
Once used by giants to carry heavily armored warriors, these grand war mammoths can easily bear more than one rider of less-than-giant stature.
Bred for their aggressive, unpredictable demeanor by the Kor'kron stablemasters, the Black War Kodos' trumpeting call signifies that blood will soon be shed.
Cherished for their heavy carrying capacity and steady gait, these stalwart beasts are the mount of choice for most native Pandaren.
A brutal aerial predator of the Voidstorm, the Sanguine Harrower makes up for its lack of stealth with a terrifying visage and hunting prowess.
Captured at a young age and raised to serve naga hunters, snapdragons are loyal and fierce companions.
To find him, drown yourself in the Circle of Stars.

In a fit of rage and despair, Thrayir conjured a storm that would ravage the land and annihilate Cyrce's enemies. After nearly ten thousand years, the seafury tempest continues to roil as an echo of his power.
This soul eater's gaze unnerves you. Best not meet its eyes for too long.
Thankfully they move fast and mostly leave the smell behind them.
What this goat lacks in size, it makes up for in stubbornness.
Moreso than normal hippogryphs, the cloudwings of Azsuna prefer to nest high up in mountain caves far above the cloud line.
A rarer, customized glider most commonly used for clandestine gatherings. Its silence makes it near impossible to detect, making it a favored tool for those who work in the shadows.
Raptors are as loyal as they are vicious. If you ain't friend, you are food. -Kijara
The pelts of young dreamstags flower with the vibrant colors of the dream.
After promising to fly you to the ends of Outland, the netherwing drake was eventually drawn to the blue skies of Azeroth as well.
It is said an elekk never forgets. No wonder it despises the Iron Horde, considering the torment the orcs put the beast through.
Under the eye of the elemental lords, many cormaera were twisted by their forces and became loyal mounts and partners.
Originating from the void, fully armored and ready for combat.
Born in the mountains of Stormheim, this terrifying fusion of storm and scale sets the sky ablaze in pursuit of its prey.
It's the third biggest murloc you've ever seen!
Almost none remain in the whole of Azeroth; only the most experienced will have seen one.
Riding a giant cylinder filled with highly explosive goblin rocket fuel all by yourself is just crazy...so bring a friend.
After being freed from vicious harpies by Cairne and Thrall, many of these creatures became valuable companions of the Horde.
Its snout is not just cold but wet. Not a pleasant way to wake up.
Tasked with keeping watch on the seas for approaching dangers, the Stormsong Coastwatchers fly constant patrols.
To evade predators, this courser dims its horn while hiding and flashes with dazzling radiance when provoked.
A gift for services rendered, this K'arroc has seen its share of hazardous flights.
The battle-hardened shell of this mighty beast can turn aside even the most hefty hammer or sharpened spear.
The Sons of Hodir believe that riding an ice-white mammoth will protect the rider from frostbite and snow blindness.
The charger's screams echo across the Maw as it continues a never-ending ride across the land, forever looking for escape from the endless torments it has been forced to endure.
This little gronnling is well-known for smashing his way into garrison inns and making a mess of the pots and pans.
A loyal steed to the Lightforged Draenei.
Even the dead need a lift every now and then.
Energetic apex hunters of Argus, the panthara hunt by sensing the energy within living things. A panthara approaching a powerful energy source will visibly change color and become more excited.
After promising to fly you to the ends of Outland, the netherwing drake was eventually drawn to the blue skies of Azeroth as well.

I have had many names throughout history, all of them spoken with dread: Neltharion, Xaxas, and many more. Yet you shall know me best as Deathwing, for so I am! I am the bane of life, the darkness within history, the lord of death, the master of destruction. And I tell you now, and so it is true, that this world is mine! - Neltharion, the Earth-Warder
Mana wyrms that are large and strong enough to support full barding and rider are quite rare and highly prized.
Human nobles have long favored this majestic breed for its beautiful golden coat and flowing white mane.
The majestic runestags are capable of siphoning anima from the ambient light of Ardenweald with their elaborate antlers. The anima is used as nourishment and to power the runestag's speed and magic.
From their infancy, Thundering Cloud Serpents are drawn to storms. They have been known to chase lightning through the blackened, roiling clouds, and to bathe in the pouring rain.
My winged children fill the skies. Not this one though.\n\n-Aviana
Once the prized possession of elite goblin society, this flying machine was sadly relegated to the scrap heap after something bigger, brighter, and more explosive arrived on the market.
This humble bee dreams of open skies. Whether or not an adventurer is along for the ride is of no consequence to it.
An ancient schematic allows for the instantiation of this early, but functional, bufonid design.
A good warhorse is loyal to its bones. Having shed its mortal coil, this steed is an omen of sickness and suffering.
According to Raptari legend, during Dazar's first ascent up the slopes of Zandalar, the soon-to-be-King was guided through the darkness by the shimmer of ivory scales and gleaming red eyes.
It takes unflagging patience and a gentle touch to train obstinate mountain goats for riding.
A particularly rare variant of slateback, "Blue Barry" was previously used as a beast of burden.
The mirror's not so you can look back, but so your foes can see something besides your tailpipes. -Rillie Spindlenut
Awakened from caves in the battlefield, and armored to the fray.
Driven mad by the void, these winged creatures are a flurry of claws and teeth.
No longer a tool of the Scarlet Crusade, this charger now guides recruits down the path of the Light with renewed purpose.
An alpha member of the herd, this kodo is a prime example of the mighty creatures which thunder through Desolace.

Preservationist Kathos encountered Pattie on her first assignment to Vol'dun. Pattie developed an affinity to Preservationist work but is eager to delve deeper, helping adventurers in their sleuthing.
One of Darmac's trained beasts, it was raised in a crucible of molten fire and shows no fear.
Umbral gorm are the most docile of all gorm, but they also grow the largest horns and mandibles. They are probably so docile because other creatures avoid riling them.
Formed from the leftover elemental energies of the Primal Storms, this magical mollusk is faster than it appears.
These high-flying denizens of Azeroth's tallest trees have developed a thick, silky coat to adapt to even the coldest climates.
It's difficult to tell because it's far too angry, but this slyvern is actually glad it's not owned by gnolls anymore.
Wily and playful in their natural habitat, ottuks possess keen eyes that can scout far afield as ably as they watch for predators.
Being the VIP of VIPs at the Gallagio has its perks, including the keys to this former King of Carnage. Cutting-edge goblin technology allows him to achieve over 100 yards per gallon!
The crane is a symbol of wisdom and nobility. Their ability to carry us into the skies is nothing short of miraculous. - Jaluu the Generous
Perhaps a little older and a bit more gray instead of customary darkened midnight, this raven still represents one of the most powerful arcane masters of Azeroth, the Guardian Khadgar.
Manifesting after Xal'atath's disappearance, this shadow's very existence begs the question: Were her schemes truly thwarted? Or have we just played deeper into her hands?

The Eversong lynxes are known for their curiosity and this one especially. Sneaking into supply stores, and treasure boxes around ritual sites has changed it forever. Anyone who manages to leash it will have a feisty mount on their hands.
This poor mule was around Drustvar when the witches took over. He's seen too much.
The acid present in the ichor of this creature sapped away the color from its shell, leaving it a striking shade of snowy white.
After Alleria and Turalyon explained the usefulness of the Draenei's long-time companion animal, the Army of the Light brought several into the fold for training.
One time a farmhand walked by without petting this goat. That's all it took for the goat to make it personal.
Corpseflies were once found throughout Maldraxxus, but many died out in the absence of anima. With anima flowing once again, they swarm.
The fiercest harrowers of Voidstorm are often twisted by the void and bound to Xal'atath's will.

Sargeras' own hound was maybe once a felstalker, but over the years the Dark Titan reforged and reshaped his companion into something much more powerful. When, at last, he was pleased with his creation, he set about creating more of the hounds, and imbuing them with shadow and flame.
Gryphons' keen eyesight allows them to see over vast distances and warn their riders of any dangers that lie ahead.
A twisted visage of a beloved companion.
A cosmic terror warped and hardened by the cruelties of the Nexus-King, now oathsworn to your service.
Raw swirling energy bound together into a cohesive form, it will only bend to the will of those strong enough to bind it.
Harika the Horrid terrorized the denizens of the Forest Ward, and with her demise her broodlings can now take this horror to denizens farther afield.
